amendments.because: Starting the new release elsewhere changed how every client starts a release and still failed when the user's own shell sits in the worktree; the pull request is already merged, so the leftover folder is only cleanup
amendments.done_when: When the pin changes mid-run, Forge starts the new release from the main checkout, so forge merge and forge land run from inside an item's worktree can remove it on Windows

amendments.because: Git may delete part of the folder before the removal fails, so Forge should not claim it kept the worktree; a held-open folder on Windows cannot be reproduced on other OSes, and a refused removal stands in for it
amendments.done_when: When forge merge or forge land can't remove an item's worktree because another program still has it open, the merge finishes, keeps the worktree and its branch, and says so

done_when: When forge merge or forge land cannot finish removing an item's worktree after its pull request merged, the merge still finishes and exits 0, says the folder could not be fully removed, and tells the user to close any program using it and run forge doctor --fix

findings.body: Raise: Not done — Forge can report that it kept the worktree after Git has deleted its files and worktree registration. This branch treats every failed `git worktree remove` as preservation, but [Git recursively deletes the directory and then removes its worktree metadata even if directory deletion fails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/builtin/worktree.c). In the stated Windows case, a process holding the root folder open can prevent the final removal after its contents have been deleted. `forge doctor --fix` discovers registered worktrees (`src/forge/doctor.py:60`), so it cannot perform the advertised cleanup once that metadata is gone.

findings.body: Raise: Test — The named proof substitutes `git worktree lock` for an open directory. Git rejects a locked worktree before deleting anything, so this test passes while the Windows failure above can leave a stripped, unregistered folder. The other named proof, `test_2`, does not force removal to fail; when the folder remains on Windows it checks only the message, not the worktree contents, Git registration, or local branch. Neither proof establishes the Done-when behavior for a worktree held open by another process.
findings.title: Not done: test a worktree held open by another process

findings.body: Raise: Gate — This new merge outcome tells the coordinator to run `forge doctor --fix`, but the change does not update `src/forge/templates/skill.md` or the worker brief. The shipped skill's merge guidance (`src/forge/templates/skill.md:60-64`) covers retained work for uncommitted changes and local commits, but not this outcome or its next step. The repository's review rule requires a same-change template update when a command's behavior or flow changes.
findings.title: Update the shipped Forge skill for the new merge cleanup step

why: On Windows, forge merge or forge land run from inside an item's worktree stops with 'could not remove the worktree' when main's pinned release changes mid-run: the old forge processes keep the worktree folder open
